key_insight: Canvas360 improves in-context panoramic generation by pairing geometry-aware pretraining with task-specific fine-tuning, making panoramic editing and synthesis more reliable. The paper also introduces a large 1M-sample dataset tailored to panoramic in-context tasks, which helps bridge the data gap.
problem_solved: Existing panoramic generation models lack enough high-quality, task-specific training data and often struggle with consistent geometry across in-context tasks like style transfer, inpainting, outpainting, and editing.
method: Two-stage framework: first geometry-aware pretraining, then downstream task-specific fine-tuning.
Canvas360Dataset: a 1M paired panoramic dataset covering multiple in-context generation scenarios.
Trains on diverse panoramic tasks to improve structural consistency and generalization across edits.
impact: This work gives practitioners a stronger foundation for building panoramic editing and generation systems that better preserve spatial structure. It is especially useful for applications in immersive media, virtual reality, and content creation workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the two-stage Canvas360 framework
Dataset overview chart illustrating the 1M paired panorama samples and task categories
Before/after panorama examples for style transfer, inpainting, outpainting, and editing
Geometry-aware consistency icon or overlay highlighting spatial alignment
paper_title: Enhancing In-context Panoramic Generation via Geometric-aware Pretraining
paper_authors: Haoran Feng, Ruiyang Zhang, Longyi Zhang, Dizhe Zhang, Lu Qi
